T2.prompt: Watch the two matching objects displayed side by side against a stationary background. Both objects remain in place, and one briefly increases in brightness before returning to its earlier appearance. Identify the side on which this brightening event occurs. Compare each object with its own appearance before and after the event, using the other object as a simultaneous reference. The relevant change is an increase in brightness over time, not the final brightness of either object. Do not choose a side because its surrounding background is lighter, because of an existing highlight, or because of the object's shape. Report the position of the object that brightened. Give your final answer as exactly one uppercase word: LEFT or RIGHT.

T3.prompt: Watch for the two objects that appear briefly side by side. During their presentation, identify each object's main long axis, meaning the direction running along its length. Compare these axes with the vertical direction of the image, as defined by its left and right edges. Decide which object's axis is closer to vertical. Use the overall elongated structure rather than a small protrusion, a surface marking, or the orientation of the background. An axis is a line, so opposite ends of the same axis do not define different orientations. Judge the objects while they are visible; their later disappearance does not change the answer. Report the side containing the more vertical axis. Give your final answer as exactly one uppercase word: LEFT or RIGHT.
